newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia-UK flights may double - Canberra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia-UK flights may double - Canberra.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said Britain and Australia had agreed to double the capacity of air services between them from April 1998.
"Flights between the United Kingdom and Australia could double over the next 18 months following a successful round of air service negotiations in London last week," Sharp said in a statement.
"The agreement also provides for a substantially liberalised route structure allowing airlines a range of new routes via third countries and to points in Europe," the minister said.
Currently, Qantas Airways Ltd and its 25-percent parent British Airways Plc each operate 14 Boeing 747 services a week between Australia and Britain.
"From next April the number of services that can be flown by each side's airlines will increase to 21 and from April 1998 to 28 services a week," Sharp said.
The bi-lateral agreement does not affect other Britain-to-Australia services offered by other countries' airlines, typically stopping in those countries.
Australia's new services need not be allocated to Qantas.
Canberra's International Air Services Commission is charged with allocating Australia's rights between Australian airlines.

However, not all of the additional flights need be completely new services. Sharp said airlines might, for example, offer a Britain-to-Australia service through the United States, using other airlines' capacity under code-sharing arrangements.
